sources.title: Constitution of Tonga, CAP. 1.01, 2020 Revised Edition
sources.notes: Byte-identical to the copy recorded in the C01 Tonga packet (789,048 bytes, same SHA-256). A consolidated edition: later amendments were not checked and nothing is backdated.

claims.text: A person convicted and sentenced to more than two years' imprisonment may not hold any office under the Government, vote for or be elected a representative unless pardoned by the King with a declaration freeing them from the disability; the disability is suspended during the 42-day appeal period and any appeal.
No person may succeed to any tofi'a or title before age 21, save members of the Royal Family, who are deemed of age at 18.

Succession to the Crown and Throne is hereditary: only those born in marriage may succeed, the eldest male child and the heirs of his body first, then the female line; fallback choices are made by the King with the consent of the nobles or by the nobles of the Assembly, the representatives of the people having no voice.

The King may appoint a Prince Regent during absence abroad; absent a declared wish, a regent for a minor heir is chosen by ballot of the Legislative Assembly in which the representatives of the people have no voice.

Giving titles of honour is the King's prerogative; hereditary titles held by chiefs of hereditary lands and by nobles of the Assembly cannot be taken away except for treason, in which case the King appoints a member of that family to succeed.
The King appoints a Privy Council composed of such people as he sees fit to call; the King in Privy Council finally determines appeals on hereditary estates and titles.

The King appoints as Prime Minister, from amongst the elected representatives, the person recommended by the Legislative Assembly under the Schedule or clause 50B; the Prime Minister holds office until another is appointed, the appointment is revoked under clause 50B, death, resignation or ceasing to be an elected representative other than by dissolution, or ineligibility.

A vote of no confidence deems the Prime Minister and all Ministers resigned. It needs five working days' notice and has no effect within 18 months after a general election, within six months before the four-year election deadline, or within 12 months of the last such motion. A replacement recommendation within 48 hours leads to appointment; otherwise the King dissolves the Assembly, an election follows within 90 days and an interim Prime Minister is appointed.

Executive authority vests in the Cabinet, collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly. The Cabinet is the Prime Minister and Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister and appointed by the King; the Prime Minister may nominate no more than four Ministers who are not elected representatives, and the Prime Minister and Cabinet must be fewer than half of the elected members excluding the Speaker.

Ministers remain until revocation on the Prime Minister's recommendation or under clause 50B, death, resignation, dismissal after impeachment or ineligibility, with a caretaker proviso after elections. A Minister who is not an elected representative sits and votes in the Assembly with a representative's rights except in a no-confidence vote. Executive authority excludes powers vested in the King or King in Council and royal prerogatives.

The Legislative Assembly comprises the representatives of the nobles, the representatives of the people and all Cabinet members. Nine nobles are elected by the nobles from their number and seventeen representatives of the people by qualified electors.
The Speaker is one of the elected representatives of the nobles, appointed by the King on the Assembly's recommendation after a Prime Minister is appointed.
No person disabled by insanity or by clause 23 may succeed to the position of a noble; every noble may vote in the nobles' election and sit if chosen.

Every Tongan subject aged 21 or more who is not a noble, not insane or imbecile and not disabled by clause 23 may, if registered, vote for the representatives of the people; a resident abroad votes only if registered and present in Tonga.

Representatives of the people are chosen by ballot; any qualified elector may nominate as a candidate in the constituency where registered, unless an outstanding court order for a specific sum remains unpaid on nomination day; an overseas resident qualifies only after three months' presence in Tonga within the six months before the election.

A by-election follows the death or resignation of a representative or deprivation after impeachment. General elections are ordinarily held every four years, the Assembly otherwise standing dissolved four years after the last general election; the King may dissolve it at pleasure and fixes the election date after consulting the Speaker.
Amendments may not affect the law of liberty, the succession to the Throne or the titles and hereditary estates of the nobles.
Hereditary estates and titles descend under a fixed law of succession to children born in wedlock, male line first, then brothers and sisters, reverting to the Crown when no lawful heir exists.

After a general election the Interim Speaker invites nominations for Prime Minister Designate, each seconded by two other elected representatives; all elected representatives of the people and of the nobles vote by secret ballot, eliminating the lowest until one candidate has more than half; the Lord Chamberlain then summons the designate for appointment. For other vacancies, except after no confidence, the Speaker follows the same procedure.

sources.title: Electoral Act, CAP. 04.08, 2016 Revised Edition
sources.notes: Consolidated edition; amendments after 2016 were not verified.

claims.text: After writs issue, the Supervisor publishes the nomination day or days, 21 to 28 days after the writ and at most two consecutive days; nominations are received at the Electoral Commission Office for Tongatapu and at the Governor's or Government Representative's office elsewhere.

A candidate for the people's seats is nominated on Form 4 signed by 50 qualified electors of the constituency, assents and declares in writing, may stand only where registered, deposits $400 that is never refunded, and delivers Supreme Court and Magistrate's Court clearances of outstanding orders under clause 65. The section does not apply to elections of representatives of the nobles.

claims.text: The Assembly comprises 17 people's representatives elected by the people and 9 nobles' representatives elected by the nobles, and after a general election nominates the Prime Minister from among its members.

sources.title: Consultation Memorandum: Seeking Stakeholder Input on a Proposed New Incorporated Societies Act (21 July 2026)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Commerce, Consumer, Trade, Innovation and Labour (MCCTIL), Tonga
sources.notes: Registry-practice evidence dated before the cutoff; it names no political party.

claims.text: Under the current Incorporated Societies Act, incorporation requires a paper application signed by five members of the proposed society with two copies of its rules and photo identification of the signatories; on incorporation the society becomes a separate legal entity with perpetual succession.
A society's rules must address the matters in section 5 of the Act, including the appointment of officers of the society and the mode of summoning and holding general meetings and voting.
claims.uncertainty: Whether any Tongan political organization is incorporated, and under what rules, is not shown; C01 records one trial testimony for the People's Party only.

sources.title: Règlement de l'Assemblée nationale; Instruction générale du Bureau; ordonnance 58-1100; lois organiques; Constitution (compilation, juillet 2025)
sources.notes: Official Assemblée compilation reproducing its rules and the Constitution with amendment notes. The Légifrance consolidation and the Conseil constitutionnel text were blocked, so this is the constitutional text read. Changes after July 2025 were not checked.

claims.text: Article 3: national sovereignty belongs to the people; electors are all adult French nationals of both sexes enjoying civil and political rights, under conditions set by law.
Article 4: political parties and groupings contribute to the exercise of suffrage and form and act freely.
Article 6: the President of the Republic is elected for five years by direct universal suffrage; no one may exercise more than two consecutive terms; an organic law sets the details.

Article 7: election by absolute majority with a second round fourteen days later between the two leading candidates; in a vacancy or definitive incapacity the President of the Senate provisionally exercises the functions and the new election is held 20 to 35 days later.
Article 8: the President of the Republic appoints the Prime Minister and, on the Prime Minister's proposal, the other members of the Government.
Article 12: after a dissolution, general elections are held 20 to 40 days later, and no new dissolution may take place in the year following those elections.
Articles 20 and 23: the Government determines and conducts national policy and is responsible to Parliament; membership of the Government is incompatible with any parliamentary mandate.
claims.locator: Constitution arts. 20 and 23, compilation PDF p. 268

claims.text: Articles 24-25: Parliament comprises the National Assembly, whose deputies (at most 577) are elected by direct suffrage, and the Senate; an organic law fixes term, membership, eligibility, ineligibilities and incompatibilities.
Article 89, last paragraph: the republican form of government cannot be the subject of a revision.

Règlement article 19: deputies may form groups by political affinity; no group may have fewer than fifteen members, not counting affiliated deputies; a group is constituted by a political declaration signed by its members with the member list and the group president's name, published in the Journal officiel.
claims.locator: Règlement art. 19, al. 1-2, compilation PDF p. 24

sources.title: Fiche de synthèse n° 3 : L'élection des députés

claims.text: Any French person of either sex aged at least eighteen, enjoying civic rights and not within a personal or professional ineligibility may stand; a candidate must meet the conditions for being an elector on the first-round date.
claims.locator: Points-clés, PDF p. 1; section II, PDF p. 4

claims.text: The 577 deputies are elected for five years by direct universal suffrage.
Since organic law no. 2014-125 of 14 February 2014, applied from the June 2017 legislative elections, local executive functions may not be combined with a deputy's mandate.
claims.locator: Section I, replacement of deputies, PDF p. 3

sources.title: Élection du Président de la République 2022 : mémento à l'usage des candidats (v. 27/01/2022)
sources.publisher: Ministère de l'Intérieur and Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères (copy hosted by the Île-de-France prefecture)
sources.edition: v. 27/01/2022; states it was submitted to the Conseil constitutionnel for opinion
sources.notes: Used for the organic-law conditions because Légifrance and the Conseil constitutionnel were blocked. Amendments between 2022 and the cutoff were not verified.

claims.text: To be eligible for President a person must be French and aged 18 (art. L. 2), have elector status (art. L.O. 127), not be deprived of eligibility by a court (arts. L. 6 and L. 199), not be under guardianship or curatorship (art. L.O. 129) and have met national-service obligations (art. L. 45); the Conseil constitutionnel checks eligibility (Constitution art. 58).

Under article 3 of Law 62-1292 of 6 November 1962 each candidate must be presented by at least 500 citizens holding listed elected offices, including members of Parliament, regional and departmental councillors and mayors.
Presenters must include elected officials of at least 30 departments or overseas collectivities, with no more than one tenth from any single one.

sources.title: Statuts du Parti socialiste (septembre 2021, congrès de Villeurbanne)
sources.edition: Cover: Septembre 2021, Congrès de Villeurbanne; file REFORME_Statuts_V9.pdf uploaded June 2026
sources.notes: Linked as the party's statutes from its reference-texts page. Amendments by later congresses were not verified.

claims.text: Membership is individual and free; the minimum age for membership is 15.
The First Secretary is the party's legal representative and presides over the National Secretariat and the Bureau national.

Save exceptions decided by the congress, no one may sit on the National Council, the Bureau national or the national conflict, financial-control or membership bodies without at least three consecutive years of membership.
The national congress meets within six months after presidential and legislative elections and also at mid-term.

Members vote on national orientation motions; a week later all members elect the First Secretary by secret ballot, the candidates being the first signatories of the two leading motions who wish to stand. After a prolonged vacancy the National Council elects a First Secretary until the next congress.

Candidates for public elective office must be paid-up members, meet electoral-code eligibility and, for national elections, the conditions of article 2.6.5; save exceptions decided by the National Council, three consecutive years of membership are required to stand in legislative, senatorial and European elections.
The party's candidate for President of the Republic is designated by a vote of members; the congress or National Council fixes the candidacy and voting arrangements.

sources.title: Règlement intérieur du Parti socialiste (4 octobre 2022)

claims.text: The internal rules implement article 3.2.7 through voter-list procedures and add no further candidacy condition for First Secretary.

sources.title: Statuts du Parti communiste français adoptés au 39e Congrès
sources.notes: Hosted on the party's asset server and linked from pcf.fr. A later congress may have amended the statutes before the cutoff; that was not verified.

claims.text: The congress meets at least every three years and whenever the National Council decides.

Governing bodies are elected by secret ballot on lists; alternative lists need 10% of congress members from at least a quarter of departments and each includes a proposed secretary; the secretary is the person whose list obtains the most votes.
All elected bodies are gender-balanced and, as a general rule, holding the same executive function is limited to nine years.
Members decide candidacies; persons convicted of attacks on human dignity, racial hatred or sexist and sexual violence may not be party candidates.
For the presidential election the national conference drafts the candidacy proposal, which is submitted to a vote of all members.

claims.text: Candidacies for the party presidency require nomination by at least 20% of the enlarged National Council; the President is elected by the ordinary General Assembly by a majority of votes cast, and the mandate ends at the next Congress.
Membership is lost by a competing candidacy, or support for one, against a candidacy presented or supported by the association.
The President may take up to twelve months' leave in the event of a presidential candidacy, the vacancy rules then applying.
